- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently under-estimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to early forecast peaks.  
- Model over-estimates late-period (last 5–7 days) prices, especially after strong sentiment shifts; apply 1–3% downward correction for final 7–10 days.  
- If sentiment shows rapid reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.8 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: over-forecasting after 3+ consecutive days of high prices; apply 1–3% downward correction if price > 1.2x recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses 1–2% of true price in the first 10 days; adjust initial 5–7 days upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
